theory.title: Question forms and indirect questions
theory.explanation: Use auxiliary inversion in direct questions. In indirect questions, keep statement word order after the question phrase: Could you tell me where she lives? Question tags repeat the auxiliary with opposite polarity.
theory.tip: Lee el contexto completo antes de elegir una forma. Comprueba el orden de las palabras y la intención del hablante.

content.passage: At a photography course, Maya met Daniel, who had recently moved to the area. She wanted to know what kind of work he did, so she asked a few friendly questions. Daniel explained that he worked in a design studio and enjoyed walking by the river. Maya asked whether he had found any good cafés nearby. He recommended one where students often met after class. Before they left, Maya said, “You come here every Thursday, don't you?” Daniel smiled and agreed. They exchanged numbers and promised to keep in touch.

content.audioTranscript: A: I wanted to discuss the message at the community course. B: Of course. Many neighbours have asked some questions. A: We meet every Thursday and invite local students. B: We can exchange phone numbers and stay in touch. A: So we have agreed to keep in contact? B: Exactly. It is easier when people communicate openly.
